targets.authors: Gino, F., Shu, L. L., & Bazerman, M. H.
targets.title: Nameless + harmless = blameless: When seemingly irrelevant factors influence judgment of (un)ethical behavior.
targets.evidence_quote: We attempted to replicate Study 2 from Gino et al. (2010). The original paper reports that people judge actions as less ethical when those actions have negative rather than positive outcomes, and when the victim is identified rather than unidentified.
targets.outcome_quote: We attempted to replicate Study 2 from Gino et al. (2010). The original result finds evidence for an outcome bias, in which influence of chance on outcomes drives observers’ ratings of a decision’s ethicality, especially when the victim is identified. This replication’s key preregistered analysis fails to reaffirm the original result.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Overall abstract verdict and discussion judge the primary preregistered replication unsuccessful. Secondary and exploratory restricted-sample results are more consistent but do not override that primary verdict.
